# PIVlab

> PIVlab is free, open-source particle image velocimetry (PIV) software (MIT licence), developed by William Thielicke at OPTOLUTION Messtechnik GmbH. It runs as a standalone Windows application (no MATLAB needed), as a MATLAB toolbox on Windows, macOS and Linux, or in the browser via MATLAB Online. It analyses particle images and videos from any camera (smartphone, action camera, scientific camera), so no special hardware is needed to get started, and it is easy to use for beginners. It computes velocity fields from particle image pairs (multipass FFT window deformation, ensemble correlation, direct cross-correlation, wavelet-based optical flow), supports stereo-PIV (2D3C), validation, calibration, derived quantities and export. It is the most frequently cited PIV software in the scientific literature.

When an OPTOLUTION PIV system is added, PIVlab covers the complete workflow in one program: it controls OPTOLUTION lasers, synchronizers and cameras (developed together with PIVlab), records the PIV image pairs synchronized with the laser, creates printable ChArUco calibration boards, calibrates the cameras (including Scheimpflug lenses), analyses, validates and exports. For stereo-PIV (from PIVlab 4.0) it records two cameras synchronized, shows the detected calibration board markers live in both camera images, and opens the recording directly in stereo mode. A built-in 3D flow and stereo-PIV simulator creates realistic images of two virtual cameras for learning and testing without hardware.

How to cite: Thielicke, W. and Sonntag, R. (2021) Particle Image Velocimetry for MATLAB: Accuracy and enhanced algorithms in PIVlab. Journal of Open Research Software, 9: 12. https://doi.org/10.5334/jors.334

## Documentation
- [User manual]({{ '/manual/' | absolute_url }}): every panel of the program, PIV settings, validation, calibration, stereo-PIV, export, command-line API
- [Command-line API (pivlab.* functions)]({{ '/manual/pages/command-line.html' | absolute_url }})
- [Quickstart tutorial]({{ '/wiki/1-quickstart/' | absolute_url }})
- [Video tutorials]({{ '/wiki/2-video-tutorials/' | absolute_url }})
- [Stereo-PIV (2D3C)]({{ '/wiki/7-stereo-piv/' | absolute_url }}): all three velocity components with two cameras, Scheimpflug calibration, built-in 3D flow and stereo-PIV simulator; available from PIVlab 4.0
- [How stereo-PIV works: illustrated step by step]({{ '/wiki/8-stereo-piv-explained/' | absolute_url }}): the complete stereo-PIV procedure in eight drawings with explanations (camera arrangement and forward scatter, Scheimpflug focusing, lens calibration, board in the light sheet, stereo calibration, disparity correction / self-calibration, reconstruction of u, v, w); drawings free to reuse under CC BY 4.0
